title: The Four Pillars — Faith, Family, Fitness & Finance | Leaving Egypt

hero.title: Four pillars that hold up a whole life.
hero.lede: Faith, Family, Fitness, and Finance aren't separate scorecards. They lean on one another—grow in one, and the others get steadier too.

intro.title: One man, four connected areas
intro.body: It's tempting to treat these like a checklist—or worse, like a measure of whether you're a "good man." That's not how they work. The pillars support each other. When your faith is steadier, you show up better at home. When your body is cared for, you have more to give. None of them is a verdict on your worth. Each is simply an area where honest, ongoing growth changes real life.

faith.title: Faith — From knowing about God to walking with Him.
faith.why: Faith is the foundation the other three pillars rest on. When a man's relationship with God is alive and honest, it steadies everything else—how he loves his family, cares for his body, and handles his money. Faith here isn't about having the right answers. It's about knowing God, trusting Him, and letting that trust shape ordinary days.
struggles: Believing the truth but rarely living it
Prayer that feels dry, rushed, or absent
Reading Scripture only in a crisis, if at all
Carrying guilt that keeps you at a distance from God
Faith that stays at church and never comes home
growth: A simple, repeatable rhythm of prayer
Reading Scripture in a way you actually understand
Confessing honestly instead of hiding
Letting God—not your performance—define your identity
Worship that shows up on a Tuesday, not just a Sunday
steps: Set a fixed five-minute time to pray each morning
Read one short passage and write down one thing it says about God
Tell one trusted brother the thing you'd rather keep hidden
Replace one scroll session with a Psalm

verse.text: Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.

reflect: Where does my life not yet match what I say I believe?
When did I last talk to God about something that actually scares me?
What would change if I truly believed what God says about me?

family.title: Family — Be someone your people can count on.
family.why: For most men, family is where character is tested daily. Your wife, children, parents, and closest people don't need a perfect man—they need a present, trustworthy one. This pillar is about learning to lead by serving: showing up with patience, listening more than you defend, and being the same man at home that you are anywhere else.
struggles: Being physically present but emotionally checked out
Reacting in anger and calling it honesty
Letting work quietly take the best of your energy
Avoiding hard conversations instead of leading them
Waiting for family to change before you do
growth: Listening without rushing to fix or defend
Owning your part and apologizing quickly
Guarding real time for the people closest to you
Leading with gentleness and steadiness, not control
Praying with and for your family
steps: Put your phone in another room during dinner
Ask your spouse or child one open question and just listen
Apologize for one specific thing without adding a "but"
Block one recurring, protected hour for family each week

verse.text: As for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.

reflect: Who in my home most needs me to be present this week?
Where do I need to apologize and haven't?
Am I leading my family with service, or managing them with control?

fitness.title: Fitness — Steward the body you were given.
fitness.why: Your body is a gift and a responsibility. This pillar isn't about a certain look, a number on a scale, or comparing yourself to anyone. It's about caring for your health so you have the energy and resilience to love and serve the people around you—sustainably, over the long haul. Small, steady habits beat short bursts of intensity every time.
struggles: All-or-nothing cycles that never last
Running on poor sleep and too much caffeine
Using exhaustion as proof of hard work
Neglecting health until something forces the issue
Tying your worth to your appearance
growth: Sustainable movement you can keep up
Better sleep and honest rest
Eating in a way that fuels rather than numbs
Strength and stamina for daily life
Caring for the body without worshiping it
steps: Set a consistent bedtime for one week
Swap one daily habit that drains you for one that restores you
Schedule the checkup you've been putting off

verse.text: Your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you.

reflect: Am I caring for my body, or just pushing it until it breaks?
What one small habit would give me more energy for the people I love?
Where has comparison crept into how I see my body?

finance.title: Finance — Handle work and money with wisdom and honesty.
finance.why: How a man handles money reveals a lot about what he trusts. This pillar is about stewardship—managing what you've been given with integrity, generosity, and a clear conscience. It is not about getting rich, growing a business, or reaching some finish line of "financial freedom." It's about being trustworthy with what's already in your hands.
struggles: Spending to soothe stress or prove something
Avoiding the numbers because they cause anxiety
Letting debt or secrecy strain your relationships
Measuring your worth by your income
Generosity that never quite happens
growth: An honest, simple picture of your money
Contentment that loosens money's grip on you
Consistent, planned generosity
Integrity in work, big and small
Peace and shared clarity with your spouse
steps: Write down what you actually spent last month
Give something intentionally, even if it's small
Have one honest money conversation with your spouse
Name one purchase you make to soothe stress—and pause it for a week

verse.text: Godliness with contentment is great gain.

reflect: What am I really trusting money to do for me?
Where is there secrecy or shame around my finances?
What would generous, honest stewardship look like this month?

finalCta.title: Pick one pillar and take one step
finalCta.lede: You don't have to fix everything at once. Tell us where you'd like to begin.
